attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, written in his own voice after he summarises the Wells Fargo report.

semantics.note: 'Pulling back from some capacity leasing' keeps his refusal to give an amount and matches the paused-leasing context.

contract.note: Reading 'walking away' as pausing or withdrawing from prospective colocation lease talks is the ordinary reading here, because the surrounding passage describes exactly that. The April 2025 window is fair.

evidence.note: Business Insider, April 22, 2025, reports the Wells Fargo note that AWS paused some colocation leasing talks. The AWS VP described it as routine capacity management, which does not deny the pauses.
CNBC, April 21, 2025, reports the same note: some lease talks paused, signed deals not cancelled. Jassy's comment about construction does not deny the lease pauses.

reviews.rationale: Reputable contemporaneous reporting of the Wells Fargo note says AWS paused some prospective colocation lease talks, which meets the support condition. Amazon's replies say demand is strong and call it routine optimisation, but they do not deny the pauses. The size of the pullback is unknown, and the speaker did not claim to know it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: Ties 'that scale' to the $3B and mass-market level discussed just before it. A firm present-tense statement about what products can do.

contract.note: Reading the scale as roughly $3B of 2025 agent sales is fair. But 'can be sold' describes capacity, so the result depends on how commercial capacity is assessed.

evidence.note: SoftBank's own disclosure of a $3B-a-year spending commitment that also covers ChatGPT Enterprise. It is not agent-only sales and does not show what existing products could deliver.
OpenAI's own disclosure that Operator was an early research preview with limitations. Plausible support for his view, but it sets no revenue ceiling.

reviews.rationale: Neither item measures agent-specific sales or what April 2025 products could have sold. The SoftBank commitment is broader than agents, and Operator's limitations do not set a sales ceiling. The packet does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: The revenue part is hedged ('it sure seems like'), so it cannot be scored. Only the firm 'certainly not making a profit' part is scorable.

contract.note: Support requires proving the hedged revenue part under a materiality measure that the speaker never gave and the contract admits it does not supply. Only the profit part should be scored. Choosing the Q4 2024 window is also the evaluator's decision.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of a $13B annual AI revenue run rate. It gives no generative-AI profit figure.
TIME reports Midjourney's 2024 revenue and that it became profitable early on. It gives no profit figure or definition for the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: The hedged revenue part is not scored. For the firm profit part, no item shows generative-AI profit or losses for any company outside OpenAI in the target period. Midjourney's earlier profitability is suggestive but not matched to the period or an accounting basis.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: The draft drops 'any kind' and 'shipping', but the contract restores both. A firm categorical statement.

contract.note: 'Any kind of autonomous computing' plainly covers bounded autonomous multistep task execution, so this is an ordinary reading, not a stretched one. A narrower reading tied to consciousness or AGI is possible but cuts against his own 'any kind'.

evidence.note: METR's independent evaluation, April 16, 2025: o3 and o4-mini agents, running commands and code, succeeded half the time on tasks that take humans 1.25 to 1.5 hours, without step-by-step human direction.
METR's April 4 Claude 3.7 report warns its results are not robust capability assessments. Even so, it reports a roughly 55-minute autonomous task horizon.

reviews.rationale: An independent April 2025 evaluation showed an OpenAI system then shipping completing multistep computing tasks on its own, which is some kind of autonomous computing. METR's caveats limit claims of general autonomy but not this bounded kind. On a narrower AGI-style reading the claim would be unresolved.
